title: Repo activity brief
instructions:
Summarise what moved in my repositories in the last 24 hours.

READ LOCAL GIT, NOT GITHUB. This is the correction that matters. Every repo here has its
origin on a self-hosted host (ssh://git@git.home.arpa:2222), and the github.com copies are
stale mirrors: on 2026-09-02 GitHub's dcode-stack was 11 days behind local, and agpack - the
top project in FOCUS.md - has no GitHub repo at all. Twenty-three runs of github-list_commits
therefore reported mirror state rather than work. Use shell git on these paths:

  /home/iconbaypark2900/jabCreative/dataScience/agpack
  /home/iconbaypark2900/openworker
  /home/iconbaypark2900/dcode-stack
  /home/iconbaypark2900/workstation-stack
  /home/iconbaypark2900/jabCreative/quantumGlobalGroup/ragtradesystem
  /home/iconbaypark2900/jabCreative/quantumGlobalGroup/sigma-trading
  /home/iconbaypark2900/jabCreative/dataScience/vqe_molecular_mcp
  /home/iconbaypark2900/jabCreative/dataScience/metered-web-broker
  /home/iconbaypark2900/jabCreative/dataScience/sentinel-local

METHOD:
  1. TODAY=$(date +%F) - take the date from the shell, never from memory.
  2. Per repo, one command:
       git -C <path> log --since=24.hours --format='%h %an %s'
     COUNT AUTHORSHIP: commits by anyone other than iconbaypark2900 are upstream tracking,
     not work in progress - the llama.cpp clones are entirely upstream. Exclude them.
  3. Only when a subject line is too terse to summarise honestly:
       git -C <path> show --stat --format= <sha> | head -20
     Do not guess what a commit did from its subject line.

ALSO FLAG:
  - UNPUSHED WORK, which is the thing most likely to be lost:
      git -C <path> log --branches --not --remotes --oneline | head -5
  - Repos with no commits in 7+ days that were active before that.
  - Commits whose message is only "WIP" or similar, with no other context.

BUDGET: at most 14 shell calls. If you hit it, say which repos you did not reach rather than
truncating silently.

OUTPUT: write repo-activity-$TODAY.md using the date from step 1. Group by repo; for each,
what changed and why it appears to matter. If nothing changed anywhere, say exactly that in
one line - do not pad it.

CONTINUITY & FOCUS — two reads, before anything else:
  1. read_file FOCUS.md in your workspace. Its first line names the week it was written for
     ("# FOCUS - week of YYYY-MM-DD"). Tag each item ON-FOCUS (bears on a project or open
     question named there) or ADJACENT. Lead with ON-FOCUS; cap ADJACENT at three and put
     them last. If FOCUS.md is missing, say so in one line and treat everything as ADJACENT.
     If the week it names is more than 8 days old, the Monday job that rewrites it did not
     run: say so in one line at the top and treat its items as weak evidence, not current
     priority. Missing fails loudly, stale fails silently, and stale is the one that happens.
  2. list_files your workspace and read your own most recent prior output. Carry forward what
     is still live, mark what has closed, and spend this run on what is genuinely NEW. Say
     "X, first flagged <date>, is now <state>" rather than rediscovering X. Never re-report
     an unchanged item as a fresh finding. The value is the running record, not a cold start.
